newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police detain 48 after Timor protest.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police detain 48 after Timor protest.

text.p: Indonesian police detained 48 youths on Sunday after a violent "anti-integration" protest at a hotel in the East Timor capital of Dili where a United Nations envoy was staying, police said.
"There was a demonstration outside the Mahkota Hotel where the envoy was staying," East Timor deputy police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters by telephone from Dili.
Rismanto confirmed there were shots fired by police during the incident but denied reports from residents that people had been killed, seriously injured or suffered broken bones.
"There were warning shots fired in the air according to the procedure laid down in the law," he said, adding there were no guhshot wounds.
Sources in the territory described the incident as "very serious" although details remained scetchy.

East Timor was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 after the abrupt withdrawal of Portuguese colonial authorities. It was annexed by Indonesia the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations and its status is disputed.

East Timor police chief Jusuf Muharam later told local journalists 48 people had been arrested and 11 required medical treatment in hospital for light injuries. The nature and cause of the injuries was not immediately clear.
Staff on duty at both Dili's general hospital and military hospital said no one had been admitted after the incident.
Rismanto said the demonstrators, numbering about 100, opposed integration with Indonesia. He said some were injured by broken glass from the hotel's windows.

The U.N. special envoy on East Timor, Jamsheed Marker, arrived in East Timor at the weekend to meet senior government and community leaders in the former Portuguese colony. He has described the trip as a "familiarisation" visit.

"I was in the room. They came at about 6 a.m. (2200 GMT Saturday) and I heard some slogans being shouted. The demonstration was then dispersed and at least some of them got into the hotel lobby. I didn't actually see the demonstration," Marker told Reuters by telephone from Dili.
Residents said the youths had wanted to meet with Marker.
"They were disastified because the U.N. envoy was only meeting with government officials and Bishop Belo," a senior community leader Manuel Carrascalao told Reuters by telephone from Dili.
Other residents said the a number of tables, chairs and glass panes in the lobby of Dili's most expensive hotel were smashed after the demonstrators entered the lobby of the hotel.
Rismanto said police quickly dispersed the protesters and Marker was able to leave on a scheduled helicopter tour of several districts in the territory.
Residents said other people later gathered at the hotel after Sunday morning services in the mostly Catholic territory but they were dispersed by police.
Rismanto said those detained were being questioned and police were looking for others involved in the incident.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan last month appointed Marker as his special assistant for East Timor after he pledged to renew talks between Indonesia and Portugal on the disputed territory's future which have achieved little in 15 years.

Marker said he had met Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo, the Jakarta-appointed Governor Abilio Soares, East Timor military chief Colonel Mahidin Simbolon and a number of community leaders since arriving in East Timor on Saturday.
